raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

TRITON_ATTN packs int8/fp8 per-token-head KV as `[K | k_scale | V | v_scale]`. The slot stride (520 B at head_size 256, 264 B at 128) and the V offset (+260/+132 B) are not multiples of 16, so `kernel_unified_attention` loads K/V one byte at a time. This PR pads each K/V half to 16 bytes. Related: #56081, #56164, #61925.

AI assistance was used: an AI coding agent wrote the code and tests under my direction, drafted this description, and automated the test and benchmark runs; I chose the approach and reviewed every changed line and the results.

## Claims

- `ld.global.b8` K/V loads: 64 → 0 (sm_86 PTX).
- `int8_per_token_head` kernel time, RTX 3080: 1.56–1.83× faster for decode at 8k–128k, 1.25–1.50× for 8-token verify and 1.65–1.96× for an 8k prefill chunk at 32k–128k; every int8 cell measured is ≥ 1.25× faster.
- End to end (TP=2, 27B hybrid, MTP): 128k TTFT −21 %, 128k decode pass 62.1 → 48.0 ms.
- Memory: +4.6 / +9.1 / +17.6 % at head_size 256 / 128 / 64 (KV pool −4.3 % in the run below). INT4 unchanged.
- Kernel outputs bit-identical to main; writer and kernels unchanged.

## Validation

**Test plan** (nightly image with this PR's files mounted):

```bash
pytest -v tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py::test_unpadded_page_size_includes_per_token_head_scales
pytest -v tests/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py
pytest -v tests/kernels/attention/test_triton_unified_attention.py -k splitk
pytest -v tests/models/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py -k int8
```

**Test result** (passed/failed/skipped):

| suite | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_kv_cache_utils.py` (per-token-head) | 1/0/0 | 4/0/0 |
| `test_per_token_kv_cache.py` | 59/23/0 | 67/21/6 |
| `test_triton_unified_attention.py -k splitk` | 25/5/0 | 25/5/0 |
| `models/quantization/test_per_token_kv_cache.py -k int8`, public mirror model | 1/0/0 | 1/0/0 |

*RTX 3080 (sm_86), 220 W cap, image `8c1434bf…5035e`, vLLM `g49cb2bbf7`, Triton 3.8.0.*

All failures are fp8 cases that also fail on main (no `fp8e4nv` on sm_86); the 6 skips are fp8 cases of the extended test, whose 12 int8/int4 cases pass. The model-level test ran with `unsloth/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct`, as we cannot access the gated meta-llama model.

Intel CI (build 14433): Quantization jobs passed; the one failing job, Benchmarks CLI (test_bench_forward: Event.__new__() got an unexpected keyword argument external), does not touch this change.

**Kernel benchmark** (`benchmarks/attention_benchmarks` with #62112, cache populated; `TRITON_ATTN`, 8 layers, block 16, CUDA graphs; per layer, median (IQR) of 5 processes, arms alternated). bf16 is main's `auto` cache; this PR does not change it (0.998–1.008× in all 12 bf16 cells).

| Hq/Hkv/D | cell | bf16 | int8 main | int8 this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12/2/256 | q1s8k | 48.8 µs | 103.9 (0.1) µs | 60.3 (0.2) µs | 1.72× |
| | q1s32k | 171.4 µs | 393.3 (18.3) µs | 215.2 (6.4) µs | 1.83× |
| | q1s128k | 667.5 µs | 1424.4 (0.6) µs | 781.2 (0.3) µs | 1.82× |
| | q8s128k | 1155.0 µs | 1772.7 (2.3) µs | 1413.7 (7.9) µs | 1.25× |
| | q8ks32k | 186.7 ms | 283.6 (0.2) ms | 144.4 (0.3) ms | 1.96× |
| | q8ks128k | 855.7 ms | 1265.5 (0.7) ms | 673.2 (3.9) ms | 1.88× |
| 32/8/128 | q1s8k | 58.4 µs | 87.2 (1.1) µs | 55.7 (0.1) µs | 1.57× |
| | q1s32k | 205.8 µs | 338.3 (1.9) µs | 216.9 (1.3) µs | 1.56× |
| | q1s128k | 814.4 µs | 1364.4 (1.0) µs | 860.2 (1.7) µs | 1.59× |
| | q8s128k | 1240.8 µs | 2023.9 (3.8) µs | 1347.4 (4.2) µs | 1.50× |
| | q8ks32k | 200.6 ms | 301.8 (0.5) ms | 166.2 (0.1) ms | 1.82× |
| | q8ks128k | 903.2 ms | 1346.0 (1.6) ms | 817.7 (1.1) ms | 1.65× |

*RTX 3080 (sm_86, 68 SMs), 220 W cap, image `8c1434bf…5035e`, vLLM `g49cb2bbf7`, Triton 3.8.0.*

**To reproduce the kernel numbers.** They need the benchmark-tool change in #62112 (int8_per_token_head support, and filling the KV cache before timing); main's tool cannot time this cache. Check out that branch, put this PR's `triton_attn.py` on top, and run:

```bash
cd benchmarks/attention_benchmarks
python benchmark.py --backends TRITON_ATTN --kv-cache-dtype {auto,int8_per_token_head} \
  --num-layers 8 --block-size 16 --head-dim {256,128} --num-q-heads {12,32} --num-kv-heads {2,8} \
  --batch-specs q1s8k q1s32k q1s128k q8s128k q8ks32k q8ks128k
```

The end-to-end numbers below need no tool change: stock `vllm serve` with the launch line given there.

#61925's single-query rule on top (not in this PR) adds up to 2.7× for kernel-level decode (12/2/256 q1s32k 220.9 → 83.3 µs, cache populated) but only ~2 % end to end below (48.0 → 47.1 ms per 128k pass): MTP verify steps have 4 query tokens, which that rule leaves at 16 segments.

**End to end.** 27B hybrid Qwen3.5-family model, W4A16 AutoRound, MTP k=3 (checkpoint `Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-MTP-W4A16-AutoRound`). Medians; 32k prompts hit ~7k cached prefix tokens in both arms. Launch line, identical in both arms (this PR's `triton_attn.py` was the only difference):

```bash
NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 vllm serve <checkpoint> --tensor-parallel-size 2 --disable-custom-all-reduce \
  --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --kv-cache-dtype int8_per_token_head \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 2 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --long-prefill-token-threshold 1024 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float16 --async-scheduling \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"max_cudagraph_capture_size":32,"custom_ops":["+rms_norm","+silu_and_mul"]}'
```

| metric | main | this PR | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| TTFT 8k / 32k / 128k (s) | 6.03 / 25.99 / 250.38 | 5.73 / 22.79 / 198.90 | 0.95 / 0.88 / 0.79 |
| N=1 decode 8k / 32k / 128k (tok/s) | 97.0 / 76.7 / 43.7 | 99.8 / 89.7 / 57.4 | 1.03 / 1.17 / 1.31 |
| N=1 ms per forward pass 8k / 32k / 128k | 29.9 / 36.1 / 62.1 | 29.0 / 33.2 / 48.0 | 0.97 / 0.92 / 0.77 |
| two concurrent 128k prompts: pair TTFT (s) / per-stream decode (tok/s) | 482.0 / 23.5 | 368.6 / 28.8 | 0.76 / 1.22 |
| MTP tokens per step, N=1 128k | 2.730 | 2.779 | |
| GSM8K n=200 accuracy | 0.96 | 0.97 | |
| 128k needle, depth 0.5 and 0.9 | retrieved | retrieved | |
| KV pool (tokens) / attention block size | 418,496 / 816 | 400,705 / 784 | 0.957 |

*2× RTX 3080 20 GB (sm_86), 220 W cap, TP=2, `--max-model-len 262144 --max-num-seqs 2 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.94`, prefix caching, image `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-x86_64@sha256:8c1434bfee7d7626eef78ef70600434ffba4a1b8813cb1d1c8707ad25f47035e`, vLLM `0.32.0rc1.dev281+g49cb2bbf7` (attention files = `fa75d3456d`), Triton 3.8.0.*

**Numerics.** With a populated cache, int8 K/V bytes, scales and prefill / decode / 4-token-verify outputs are bit-identical to main (12/2/256, 32/8/128; kernel probe on one RTX 3080, same image). Model logprobs (30,617-token document) differ from main by 0.0224 nats mean abs (99.9 % top-1 agreement) only because the hybrid model's attention block size follows the page size (816 → 784); with `--block-size 816` they are bit-identical. Against a bf16-KV reference: main 0.02181, this PR 0.02198 nats, paired +0.00017 (95 % CI −0.00032 to +0.00068), non-inferior.

## Details

**Root cause.** Triton 3.8.0 marks an argument 16-divisible only if `arg % 16 == 0` / `data_ptr() % 16 == 0` (`triton/backends/compiler.py:75-92`). Offline compile of `kernel_unified_attention` (3D, D=256, GQA 6, TILE 16, 4 warps):

| layout | slot stride | V offset | `ld.global.v4.b32` | `ld.global.b32` | `ld.global.b8` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bf16 KV | 512 B | – | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| int8 per-token-head, main | 520 B | 260 B | 4 | 24 | 64 |
| int8 per-token-head, this PR | 544 B | 272 B | 4 | 4 | 0 |

*sm_86 compile, image `8c1434bf…5035e`, Triton 3.8.0; the RTX 3080 benchmark runs JIT-compiled the same counts.*

The kernel test missed this (separate aligned K/V tensors, 2D path only). It now reads the packed cache, runs `seq_threshold_3D` ∈ {0, 8} with a q=4 batch, and asserts split-K ran.

**Change.** `customize_spec` sizes each INT8/FP8 half as `round_up(head_size * dtype_size + 4, 16)`; `_ensure_scale_caches` takes `head_size` from the layer. Scale placement and the `content // 2` split are unchanged.

| head_size | bytes per token and KV head | change | vs bf16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 136 → 160 | +17.6 % | 0.53 → 0.63 |
| 128 | 264 → 288 | +9.1 % | 0.52 → 0.56 |
| 256 | 520 → 544 | +4.6 % | 0.51 → 0.53 |

*Computed by `customize_spec`; the RTX 3080 runs above (image `8c1434bf…5035e`, Triton 3.8.0) saw 544/288 B strides.*

**Alternative: one pad.** `[K | V | k_scale | v_scale | pad]` (528/272/144 B, +1.5/+3.0/+5.9 %) also removes every byte load and passes the same tests. Cache populated (n=5 processes per arm): 8k prefill chunks at head_size 256 take 9–17 % less time with this PR (q8ks32k/q8ks128k at 12/2, 24/4); decode and verify match within ±3 % except 32/8/128 q1s8k (this PR −7 %). Hence two pads; one pad is ready if reviewers prefer a smaller cache.

**Related.**
- #56081: same misalignment in a gather-based sparse kernel (sm_121) needing 128-byte alignment or side tensors; not fixed here.
- #56164 is not a duplicate: it opts out of inline scales, this PR pads them. They conflict in `customize_spec` and `_ensure_scale_caches` but compose (its early return stays first).
- Inline packing from #36893 (closed PR) / #38378 (merged PR) is kept.

**Layout change.** Persisted offload stores and prefill/decode pairs on different versions are invalid across this PR. On hybrid models the attention block size follows the page size (816 → 784 above).

**Limits.**
- Measured only on RTX 3080 (sm_86, power-capped); A100, L4 and H100 not measured; PTX compiled only for sm_86.
- fp8 per-token-head shares the layout code but cannot run on sm_86; not timed.

**CI.** No sm_86 runner. `test_per_token_kv_cache.py` runs in the H200 Quantization step (`.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml:5`), attention kernel tests on L4 (`kernels.yaml:315`).

**Duplicate search** (2026-10-16):

```bash
gh issue view 56081 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "56081 in:body"               # #56164
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "int8_per_token_head"          # no layout PR
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "inline scales customize_spec" # #56164
```

**Change.** `customize_spec` sizes each INT8/FP8 half as `round_up(head_size * dtype_size + 4, 16)`; `_ensure_scale_caches` takes `head_size` from the layer. Scale placement and the `content // 2` split are unchanged.

| head_size | bytes per token and KV head | change | vs bf16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | 136 → 160 | +17.6 % | 0.53 → 0.63 |
| 128 | 264 → 288 | +9.1 % | 0.52 → 0.56 |
| 256 | 520 → 544 | +4.6 % | 0.51 → 0.53 |

*Computed by `customize_spec`; the RTX 3080 runs above (image `8c1434bf…5035e`, Triton 3.8.0) saw 544/288 B strides.*

**Alternative: one pad.** `[K | V | k_scale | v_scale | pad]` (528/272/144 B, +1.5/+3.0/+5.9 %) also removes every byte load and passes the same tests. Cache populated (n=5 processes per arm): 8k prefill chunks at head_size 256 take 9–17 % less time with this PR (q8ks32k/q8ks128k at 12/2, 24/4); decode and verify match within ±3 % except 32/8/128 q1s8k (this PR −7 %). Hence two pads; one pad is ready if reviewers prefer a smaller cache.

**Related.**
- #56081: same misalignment in a gather-based sparse kernel (sm_121) needing 128-byte alignment or side tensors; not fixed here.
- #56164 is not a duplicate: it opts out of inline scales, this PR pads them. They conflict in `customize_spec` and `_ensure_scale_caches` but compose (its early return stays first).
- Inline packing from #36893 (closed PR) / #38378 (merged PR) is kept.

**Layout change.** Persisted offload stores and prefill/decode pairs on different versions are invalid across this PR. On hybrid models the attention block size follows the page size (816 → 784 above).

**Limits.**
- Measured only on RTX 3080 (sm_86, power-capped); A100, L4 and H100 not measured; PTX compiled only for sm_86.
- fp8 per-token-head shares the layout code but cannot run on sm_86; not timed.

**CI.** No sm_86 runner. `test_per_token_kv_cache.py` runs in the H200 Quantization step (`.buildkite/test_areas/quantization.yaml:5`), attention kernel tests on L4 (`kernels.yaml:315`).

**Duplicate search** (2026-10-16):

```bash
gh issue view 56081 --repo vllm-project/vllm --comments
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "56081 in:body"               # #56164
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "int8_per_token_head"          # no layout PR
gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "inline scales customize_spec" # #56164
```
